_header: GRANDFATHERED: every registered resource that, as of 2026-09-10, the
PRODUCT cannot remove a record from -- no `delete` and no `soft_delete`
verb in api/_resources/*.js EXTRA_ACTIONS.
THESE ARE NOT APPROVED. They are VISIBLE. The list exists so that
tools/removal_path_check.py can fail on a NEW one instead of sitting at
exit 1 forever and gating nothing -- the failure preauth_oracle_check's own
open-work row already names about itself. Same shape and same intent as the
pre-2026-08-29 list in tools/employee_auth_guard_check.py, whose header
says it plainly: not fixed, only visible, and meant to be burned down
rather than added to.
WHY THIS IS NOT A SOFT NUMBER. If these were collection rows -- one row per
licence holding a JSON array -- removing an item would be an ordinary write
and none of it would matter. They are not. api/sd-data.js writes
`on_conflict=license_hash,<id_col>` at 117 call sites, one row per RECORD,
against THREE single-row collection upserts on the whole platform
(msb_sale_hours, sd_public_shop, sd_shared_knowledge). A write touches only
its own keyed row, so writing the collection without an item removes
nothing.
WHAT IS ALREADY EXCLUDED AND WHY, so this list is not read as the whole
picture: 50 resources declare a removal verb (SAIRNcode 28/28, StoneDesk
21/36, SAIRNdental 1/24); 2 are single-row collections; 13 are called
APPEND-ONLY by their own registry comment, which is a real reason and is
read rather than re-decided.
TO BURN ONE DOWN: give the resource a removal verb and its server-side
gate, or replace its line here with a REAL REASON. `append-only by design`
is a real reason. `nobody has needed it yet` is also a real reason and is
better than silence. What is not acceptable is leaving it here because the
line already exists.
THE CONSEQUENCE THIS MEASURES: a row the product can create is a row only
Michael can remove, by hand, in the Supabase SQL editor. That is what the
15+ sql/*_cleanup.sql files across 11 apps are, and why that pile keeps
growing.
BURN-DOWN LOG. 2026-09-11: three entries left this list by being labelled
APPEND-ONLY in their own registry comment after their writers were read --
dnt_charges, dnt_payments (one push-only write call each, no edit path, no
remover) and sv_audit_log (logDoseAudit pushes only, and the app's own
comment says rewriting the trail is the one thing forbidden). Two more
traded silence for a REASON without leaving the list: law_trusttx and
alf_incidents are UPDATED in place, so append-only would be false of them,
but deletion is forbidden by design and now says so.
AND THE METHOD THAT DID NOT WORK, recorded so it is not repeated: deriving
append-only-ness mechanically failed TWICE in the PERMISSIVE direction. A
scan for `xData('write','<resource>',...)` found no writer for 22 of the 56
Tier A rows, because SAIRNvet writes through a variable key
(svData('write', key, rec)) and SAIRNbiz writes through st() with a backup
hook -- blind zeros, not evidence. And a scan for an edit path keyed on
`.map(` plus an edit id called law_trusttx and alf_incidents CREATE-ONLY
when both mutate a find()ed object in place. Either false positive would
have labelled a mutable record append-only and exempted it silently.
Label from a read of the writer, never from a scan or a table name.

grandfathered.law_trusttx: NOT append-only -- confirmVoid() mutates the row in place (status, voided_reason, voided_at) -- but DELETION IS FORBIDDEN BY DESIGN. A void is a status change on the original transaction, never a removal, so the client ledger stays reconstructable and clientLedgerBalance() can be recomputed from the rows. Destroying an attorney trust-account entry is a bar-reportable act, not a data-hygiene choice. Verified 2026-09-11 by reading saveTrustTransaction() and confirmVoid() in sairnlaw.html.
